evidence: Sall. Cat. 37.7: manuum mercēde inopiam tolerāverat, had kept poverty off with the wages of their hands
Traupman 403: mercēdem accipere, to receive wages; mercēdem tribuere, to pay wages
M-O s.v. salary, pay (of employees), wages
terms.comment: What any work earns: a labourer’s wages, a teacher’s fee, an actor’s pay; also rent (see rent, money paid for a house or flat). A day’s wage is mercēs diurna: mercēde diurnā conductum, a man hired by the day (Hor. S. 2.7.18).

evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.198: īnfimī hominēs mercēdulā adductī, the lowest of men, drawn by a little pay

phrases.latin: ingrāta es, inquit, ōre quae nostrō caput incolume abstulerīs et mercēdem postulēs
phrases.english: ‘Ungrateful creature,’ he said, ‘you got your head out of my mouth unharmed, and now you want paying?’

phrases.latin: dignus enim est operārius mercēde suā
phrases.english: for the labourer deserves his wages
to receive (fair, good, low, unfair) wages
